key_insight: A coupled simulation-and-ANN framework can accurately predict and optimize friction stir welding quality in HDPE by linking process settings to temperature, force, and defect formation.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process maps for selecting rotational speed, welding speed, and preheating conditions to improve weld integrity and reduce wormhole defects in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model for HDPE friction stir welding
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental time-series data
Process-parameter sweep over rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating
evidence_signal: The CEL model matched experiments on voids, thermal response, and forces, while the ANNs achieved R2 values of 0.91 to 0.99 for temperature and axial force prediction.
watch_item: The reported optimization is based on the tested HDPE parameter space, so transfer to other materials, tool designs, or thicknesses may require retraining and revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
